- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in next 5–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at 1–2 days above true peak, then allow gradual decline.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model overestimates mean — adjust downward by 2–5% for 3–5 day horizon.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative and price is trending down, model often fails to recognize mean reversion — add 1–3% downward bias for 7–10 day horizon.  
- When sentiment is positive and price is rising, model tends to overestimate momentum — reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.  
- Model often ignores sentiment volatility — if sentiment swings sharply, adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag in reaction to sentiment shifts.
